summary: Cascade Crest summit lookout: a cupola cabin built in 1923 (camp from 1920); burned in 1955 or removed in 1958 per sources that differ; metal parts remain.

facts.status_note: Burned in the fall of 1955 per Rex's page and Willhite; the register, firelookout.com and Wikipedia date removal or destruction to 1958. A hiking guide says metal parts remain.

staffing.status: last staffed 1942 by James Stearns; named lookouts include Ed Mahn (1912, 1921) and Charles Bowers (1913, 1914)

access.note: Reached on foot from a small trailhead on a dirt road near Willamette Pass, as a hiking guide describes the route. No Forest Service page was checked.

visit.trail_note: Park at a small trailhead on a dirt road near Willamette Pass; the trail climbs to the Pacific Crest Trail and on to the summit

events.note: Rex's page: observation point for fire detection, with no improvements at the time; Willhite: a camp used for observation
Ed Mahn the lookout on Maiden Peak; a telephone line from Crescent reached the summit
Charles Bowers stationed on the summit for the summer
Camp set up on the summit, per the register and firelookout.com
Station discontinued for the year (Rex's page)
Cupola cabin replaced the camp; Jim Gauldon of Bend to build it for about $650 (Bend Bulletin item quoted by Rex's page)
James Stearns, the last person to staff the lookout
District Ranger Tom Greathouse and Ray Koski burned the lookout house in the fall (Rex's page and Willhite)
Register says removed in 1958, firelookout.com says destroyed in 1958, Wikipedia says removed in 1958

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page and Willhite say District Ranger Tom Greathouse and Ray Koski burned the lookout house in the fall of 1955. The register, firelookout.com and Wikipedia date its removal or destruction to 1958. The story reports both accounts.
Rex's page and Willhite put observation use of the summit in 1908. The register and firelookout.com date the first camp to 1920. The story reports both dates.

notes_for_editor: Elevation in the brief (2,382.9 m) matches the register's 2,383 m; FFLOS registration date May 11, 2011 matches the register. The removal date conflict (1955 burning vs 1958 removal) is unresolved in the sources and is reported in the story. The summit condition relies on a single undated photo caption ('Metal parts of lookout remain') from a hiking guide. The access level 'public' is inferred from the hiking guide's trail description; no Forest Service page was checked, so the editor may want to confirm before publication. The 1908 observation use and the 1920 first camp are both reported as the sources give them.
